title: Data governance: quality, lineage, metadata and ownership

videos.script: Twenty-three of Ipê's customers have never received an e-mail. Their addresses have no at sign, and the site took them anyway. Seven more end in dot con. {{emails}} Twelve people signed up twice. Three orders are dated next year. And thirteen hundred customers consented to marketing before their account existed. {{findings}} None of this was found by looking. It was found by asking the data six questions, each with a number for an answer. {{measure}} This lesson is about what happens next. Who decides what each finding means, because fourteen orders with no customer turn out to be exactly right. {{owners}} Rules that ask the same questions every day and keep every answer. A constraint that stops the next bad address at the door, without first fixing the old ones. {{rules}} And the two maps every data team needs: what each column means, and where each one goes. {{maps}} Governance is the answer to who decided this, and where is it written. {{end}}
